- .github/workflows/ci.yml:2267-2274 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The alphabetical order of the test file list is broken by inserting test_check_workflow_script_refs.py and test_ci_actionlint_install_retry.py out of order.
  WHY: Gemini says tests/test_ci_inventory_parity_order_contract.py enforces alphabetical order, so CI fails. Minimax says no test enforces it and rates it NIT. Severity disagreement: the highest (major) is used.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:7035-7038 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: scripts/gh_helpers.sh is sourced and gh_retry is defined inconsistently between mark-stable.yml and test-and-mark-stable.yml.
  WHY: test_dispatch_step_bodies_match_across_workflows expects identical dispatch step bodies. Minimax disputes this finding in its output, saying both files carry the same lines at mark-stable.yml:1362-1363 and test-and-mark-stable.yml:7038-7039.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:238-251 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: load_expected_templates() unconditionally unions every full-profile wrapper into the expected set, so core-profile consumers lacking review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml and unblock_judge_dispatch.yml are reported as drifting with missing=true.
  WHY: This produces false-positive drift alerts. Severity disagreement: Gemini says MAJOR, the others say NIT; the highest is used.
- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:1409-1415 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: GH_RETRY_IDEMPOTENT=true retries the repository_dispatch POST, which has no dedup key, so duplicate consumer updater runs are possible. The same pattern is at test-and-mark-stable.yml:7087-7091.
  WHY: A lost response after an accepted dispatch can launch duplicate update_workflows runs. Minimax says a consumer-side concurrency group mitigates this; Luna says the updater has no concurrency group and a competing run fails the branch lease check.
- README.md:1189-1192 | severity=nit | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The README says the audit checks only ai-*.yml wrappers, but the script now also checks the wrappers listed in profiles/full.txt.
  WHY: Operators will not expect reports of missing or stale dispatch wrappers.

  WHY: Consumers on the core profile are flagged for wrappers their profile does not ship. The audit has no per-consumer WORKFLOW_PROFILE lookup.
- Minimax's cross-pollination note disputes Gemini's dispatch-step finding. It says both workflows carry identical source and type gh_retry lines at mark-stable.yml:1362-1363 and test-and-mark-stable.yml:7038-7039.
